title: Longest Common Prefix
statement:
Find the longest prefix that every word in a list starts with.

The first line is the number of words `n`, and the second line holds the `n` words, made of lowercase letters and separated by spaces. A prefix is a run of letters at the start of a word, so `fl` is a prefix of `flower`. Print the longest prefix that all the words share. When they share none, or the list is empty (`0` and an empty line), print `none`. A list with a single word prints that whole word.

Input:

```text
3
flower flow flight
```

Expected output:

```text
fl
```
hints: The shared prefix can never be longer than the shortest word, so you can stop as soon as any word runs out of letters.
Go through the first word one position at a time, and check that every other word has the same letter at that position.

As soon as a word is too short or has a different letter at position `i`, the answer is the first `i` letters of the first word. Each language cuts that piece out for you: `word[:i]` in Python and Go, `slice` or `substring` in JavaScript, `substring` in Java, `substr` in C++.
